svg.title: Fig 3 — two candidates against the validation split (n=4 per side)
svg.desc: Two promotion decisions, one per block. The first candidate was accepted with an efficiency-only caveat; the second, written under the structural bound, was rejected because no declared objective improved. In both, all ten behavioural counters are identical before and after; what moves is tokens and latency.
svg.text: Two candidates against the validation split — n=4 per side
Behavioural counts unchanged; single run against a shared hosted endpoint. The acceptance rests on tokens and latency alone.
identical on all ten counters in both runs
Checks applied by the promotion gate
latency 25.387 vs 89.219 s per episode (0.28×, ceiling 1.5×)
baseline reviewer-v1 · candidate reviewer-v2 · cost unknown, so the token ceiling is the effort bound that was applied
Second candidate cand-c9880d02f1f4 (structural bound): REJECTED — no declared objective improved.
Every no-regression check passed and nothing improved, so the gate refused it. Note the latency axis: this comparison's slowest episode is far below the first comparison's.
identical on all ten counters in both runs
axis ends at 60 s, not 300 s
Checks applied by the promotion gate
latency 27.478 vs 25.513 s per episode (1.08×, ceiling 1.5×)
baseline reviewer-v1 · candidate reviewer-v2 · cost unknown, so the token ceiling is the effort bound that was applied
prompts/ACTIVE_REVIEWER stays reviewer-v1: the first decision was accepted with a caveat and left pending a repeat comparison, the second was rejected, and neither moved the pointer
A rejection is a real outcome, not a failed run (spec 8.7): a candidate that improves completion by relaxing a boundary is what this gate exists to stop

the two blocks are not a like-for-like comparison of the two candidates: they ran against different dataset versions (val-2026-09-13.1 and val-2026-09-13.2), each against its own contemporaneous baseline
cost: unknown (no verified model prices); both decisions are measured in tokens and seconds only
sample_count=4: a small manually reviewed fixture corpus, not a statistically powered safety study (spec 8.2)
n=4 per side: zero observed failures is not a zero failure probability (spec 9.2: do not select a lucky run while suppressing the others)
